mainTopic: Selling פסולי המוקדשין and מעשר בהמה: הקדש's benefit at redemption, the orphans' exception, quoting teachings in the speaker's name, and הבלעה
overview: The גמרא first asks when the משנה's rule applies, that the benefit from פסולי המוקדשין goes to הקדש. Before פדיון does not work for everyone, because a slaughtered animal cannot undergo העמדה והערכה. So the case is after פדיון: הקדש gains because the owner pays more at redemption, knowing he may later sell the meat in the market. Next, the גמרא asks how מעשר בהמה can be sold at home when a ברייתא says it may never be sold. רב ששת answers that the משנה speaks of orphans' מעשר, allowed to prevent their loss. The גמרא then tells how his attendant repeated this without credit, and explains why being quoted matters: a quoted scholar's lips move in the grave. Finally, it quotes the ברייתא about orphans' מעשר and הבלעה, and אביי and רבא disagree on how to read it. רבא proves that the Torah bans selling מעשר only while the animal is alive. The ban after שחיטה is a rabbinic גזירה, and his explanation of its limits continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and asking when it applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the benefit from פסולי המוקדשין goes to הקדש, and asks: at what stage?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'All disqualified consecrated animals, their benefit goes to the Temple.' When?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks at what point in time it applies. This sets up the next steps, which will test each possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished קדשים animal has two stages: before it is redeemed and after it is redeemed. The גמרא wants to know which stage the משנה means when it says 'the benefit goes to הקדש.'

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became unfit for the altar, usually because of a blemish
Their benefit or profit
The Temple treasury or consecrated property
When? At what stage?

phrases.english: Gemara:
All disqualified consecrated animals
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: their benefit goes to the Temple treasury.
When does this apply?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's rule that the benefit goes to הקדש applies before or after the animal's פדיון

steps.title: After redemption, the profit belongs to the owner
steps.stepSummary: The first option, after פדיון, is rejected: once the animal is redeemed, the profit belongs to the owner, not to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it applies after its redemption, does the benefit go to the Temple? The benefit belongs to the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, that the משנה refers to after the animal was redeemed. It immediately shows that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner pays הקדש to redeem the animal, the animal becomes his חולין property. Any profit from selling it afterward is his. So the משנה's phrase 'benefit to הקדש' does not seem to fit this stage.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Its redemption, meaning buying it out of הקדש with money
The owners

phrases.english: If you say: after its redemption —
does their benefit go to the Temple?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: certainly not

phrases.english: Their benefit belongs to the owner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question and rejects it
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה refers to after פדיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After פדיון the animal is the owner's property, so the profit cannot belong to הקדש

steps.title: Suggesting the case is before redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes the other option: the משנה refers to before פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it applies before its redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the second option: the משנה means before the animal is redeemed. This sets up a new problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before פדיון the animal still belongs to הקדש. So the money paid to make it חולין would naturally go to הקדש, which fits the משנה's words.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switches to a new suggestion)
Before

phrases.english: Rather, before its redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'after פדיון' reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה refers to after פדיון
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to before פדיון, when the animal still belongs to הקדש

steps.title: A slaughtered animal cannot be appraised
steps.stepSummary: Before פדיון the animal cannot be slaughtered first, because redemption requires העמדה והערכה, which needs a live animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says they are slaughtered? Redemption requires standing and valuation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'before פדיון' reading. The משנה says the animals are slaughtered in the market, but a dead animal cannot be stood up and appraised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem a consecrated animal, it must be stood before a כהן alive so he can set its value (ויקרא כז). If the animal is slaughtered before פדיון, this can no longer be done. So the משנה's case cannot be before פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: They are slaughtered (a word from the משנה)
Standing the live animal before a כהן and having him appraise it
It requires

steps.confusionAlert: 'נשחטין' is not a new rule here. It is a word the גמרא is quoting from the משנה ('they are slaughtered in the market') in order to challenge the 'before פדיון' reading.

phrases.english: But they are slaughtered (in the market)?
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: But it requires standing and valuation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'before פדיון' suggestion
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה refers to before פדיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before פדיון the animal must stay alive for העמדה והערכה, so it cannot be slaughtered first as the משנה describes

steps.title: The problem depends on a dispute about appraisal
steps.stepSummary: The challenge only works for the view that קדשי מזבח need העמדה והערכה, and that view still needs an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that altar-consecrated items were not included in standing and valuation. But for the one who says they were included, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that one opinion avoids the problem, but the other opinion does not. So the 'before פדיון' reading still does not work for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute about whether קדשי מזבח that became blemished need העמדה והערכה. If they do not, the animal could be slaughtered and then redeemed, and 'before פדיון' works. But according to the opinion that they do, the problem from step 4 remains, so the גמרא needs another explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
Included in
What is there to say? (asks for an explanation; the next step gives one)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
that items consecrated for the altar were not
included in standing and valuation,
but according to the one who says
they were included in standing and valuation,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge of step 4 to one opinion but keeps it standing
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'before פדיון' reading, according to the view that קדשי מזבח need העמדה והערכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view the slaughtered animal cannot be redeemed, so the 'before פדיון' reading fails for at least one opinion
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא wants a reading of the משנה that works for every opinion, not just one.

steps.title: After redemption; the gain to הקדש comes at the original redemption
steps.stepSummary: The case really is after פדיון. 'Benefit to הקדש' means that הקדש gains at the start, through a higher redemption price.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it actually applies after redemption. And what does 'their benefit goes to the Temple' mean? It refers to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first option, after פדיון, and explains the משנה's phrase in a new way. This is the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is redeemed alive, so there is no appraisal problem, and then it is slaughtered and sold. 'Benefit to הקדש' does not mean the market profit goes to הקדש. It means that because the animal may be sold freely in the market, the owner pays more at the original redemption, and הקדש collects that higher price.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (returns to an earlier option)
And what does it mean?
Regarding the beginning, meaning the original redemption

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה refers to after פדיון. The owner keeps the market profit. הקדש benefits because the market privilege raises the price at the original redemption.

phrases.english: Rather, it actually refers to after redemption,
and what does 'their benefit goes to the Temple' mean?
It refers to the beginning (the initial redemption).
phrases.notes: Because the animal may be sold in the market, its redemption value is higher

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons the 'before פדיון' reading and reinterprets the משנה's phrase to answer step 2's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Benefit to הקדש' means the money from the market sale goes to הקדש
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Benefit to הקדש' means the higher price הקדש receives at the original redemption
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פסולי המוקדשין are redeemed alive and then sold in the market. הקדש's benefit is the increased value at the time of פדיון.

steps.title: Why market permission raises the redemption price
steps.stepSummary: The owner knows he may later sell the redeemed animal at full market value, so he is willing to pay more to הקדש when he redeems it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Sage permits them to be sold in the market, slaughtered in the market, and weighed by the pound, the owner will pay more to redeem the animal in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step. It explains exactly how הקדש gains even though the sale happens after פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat sold in the busy butchers' market by weight brings a better price. The owner knows this ahead of time, so he will offer more money when he redeems the animal. That extra money goes to הקדש, and this is the 'benefit to הקדש' the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: The butchers' market, where meat is sold publicly
A litra (pound), a unit of weight used to sell meat
At the start, from the beginning
He redeems

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'benefit to הקדש' happens at the moment of redemption. The owner pays more because he expects to sell the meat in the market later.

phrases.english: For since the Master permits them
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: to be sold in the butchers' market
and slaughtered in the butchers' market
and weighed by the litra,
he adds more and redeems it at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the answer in step 6 works: why הקדש gains at the start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After פדיון, all profit belongs to the owner, so הקדש cannot gain anything.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש gains through a higher redemption price, because the owner expects to sell the meat freely later.

steps.title: How can מעשר be sold even at home?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה suggests that בכור and מעשר may be sold at home but not in the market. That makes sense for בכור, but how can מעשר be sold at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: except for בכור and מעשר, whose benefit belongs to the owner. Granted, a בכור may not be sold in the market but may be sold at home. But מעשר, can it be sold even at home?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It questions the hint that מעשר may be sold at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only excludes בכור and מעשר from the market. That implies both may still be sold privately at home. This is fine for בכור, but the גמרא doubts that מעשר may be sold anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to the כהן
Here: מעשר בהמה, the tenth animal set aside as a sacrifice
Their benefit belongs to the owners
Granted; this part makes sense
In his house (a private sale)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not openly say 'they may be sold at home.' The גמרא reads that out of the fact that the משנה only bans the market.

phrases.english: Except for the firstborn and the tithe
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: whose benefit belongs to the owners.
Granted, a firstborn:
it is in the market that it may not be sold,
but in his house it may be sold.
But the tithe:
may it be sold in his house?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and starts a new question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's hint that מעשר may be sold at home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing a sale at home seems to clash with the rule that מעשר may never be sold.

steps.title: A ברייתא says מעשר can never be sold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בכור may be sold while alive, but מעשר may not be sold in any form.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: about בכור it says 'You shall not redeem,' yet it may be sold alive. About מעשר it says 'It shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold at all: not alive or slaughtered, not unblemished or blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source behind the question. It shows that מעשר may not be sold in any situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals have a 'no redemption' verse, but the ברייתא treats them differently. A בכור may still be sold while alive, but מעשר may not be sold at all. Since 'blemished and slaughtered' is included, the משנה's case of blemished meat sold at home seems forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradiction)
'You shall not redeem' (the verse about בכור)
'It shall not be redeemed' (the verse about מעשר)
Unblemished
Blemished

steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'not blemished' close every escape route. Even the משנה's own case, a blemished animal, falls under the ban.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
Regarding a firstborn it is stated 'You shall not redeem,'
yet it may be sold alive;
regarding the tithe it is stated 'It shall not be redeemed,'
and it may not be sold,
neither alive nor slaughtered,
neither unblemished nor blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that makes the question in step 8 hard.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר may not be sold even at home
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on the verse 'לֹא יִגָּאֵל'

steps.title: רב ששת: the case is מעשר belonging to orphans
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה is talking about orphans' מעשר. The sale was allowed so the orphans would not lose the meat, as a form of השבת אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת found this hard at night and answered it in the morning from a ברייתא: we are dealing with מעשר בהמה belonging to orphans, and the חכמים allowed it because of השבת אבידה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the contradiction. He narrows the משנה to a special case where a home sale is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally מעשר may never be sold, and that rule still stands. Young orphans cannot eat a whole animal before the meat spoils. So the חכמים made an exception and allowed a sale, to protect them from loss, just as one returns a lost item. The ban on מעשר stays in place; this is only an exception for one case.

keyTerms.meaning: At night, in the evening
In the morning, early
Orphans
We are dealing with (limits the case)
Returning a lost item; here, preventing someone's loss
They touched it, meaning they made a rule about it

steps.whatToRemember: Normally, מעשר may never be sold. The משנה's home sale is a special exception for orphans, made to prevent their loss.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean מעשר may be sold in general. It is a narrow exception made by the חכמים. Even for the orphans, the sale stays at home, not in the market.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיקַּשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּאוּרְתָּא,
phrases.english: This matter was difficult for Rav Sheshet at night,
and he resolved it in the morning from a baraita:
we are dealing with animal tithe belonging to orphans,
and because of returning a lost item they ruled on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיקַּשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא) to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to allow selling any blemished מעשר at home, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only orphans' מעשר. The חכמים allowed its sale to prevent the orphans' loss, while the general ban stays.

steps.title: רבי אידי repeats רב ששת's teaching without credit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אידי, רב ששת's attendant, repeated רב ששת's answer in the בית מדרש without naming him. רב ששת was upset and cursed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אידי, the attendant of רב ששת, heard this answer from him. He went and said it in the בית מדרש, but he did not say it in רב ששת's name. רב ששת heard about it and was upset. He said: 'Whoever stung me, let a scorpion sting him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about the answer רב ששת just gave about orphans' מעשר. His attendant repeated it publicly without saying where it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha does not change here. The story shows that quoting a teaching without naming its author is a real wrong, strong enough that רב ששת reacted with a curse. This sets up the question in the next step: why did it bother him so much?

keyTerms.meaning: His attendant or personal assistant
The study hall
In his name, giving him credit
He was upset or annoyed
A scorpion

phrases.english: Rabbi Idi, the attendant of Rav Sheshet,
heard it from him.
phrases.notes: 'It' means רב ששת's explanation about orphans' מעשר (step 10).

phrases.english: He went and said it in the study hall,
but he did not say it in his name.
Rav Sheshet heard and was upset.
He said: The one who stung me,
let a scorpion sting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִידִי סַרְסְיֵהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה שַׁמְעַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about how רב ששת's answer from step 10 was passed on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating a teaching without crediting its author upset רב ששת deeply.

steps.title: Why did רב ששת care about credit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it made to רב ששת whether the teaching was said in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רב ששת, what difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב ששת was so upset. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of Torah is spread either way, so it looks like a matter of personal honor. The גמרא assumes a תלמיד חכם would not be this upset over honor alone, so there must be a deeper reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב ששת's reaction in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being quoted by name mattered so much to רב ששת.

steps.title: רב's difficulty with the verse 'I will dwell in Your tent forever'
steps.stepSummary: To answer, the גמרא quotes רב, who asks about the פסוק 'אגורה באהלך עולמים': how can a person live in two worlds?
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'I will dwell in Your tent עולמים (worlds)'? Is it possible for a person to live in two worlds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting רב, who points out a problem in a פסוק from תהלים. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עולמים is plural, so it sounds like דוד asked to live in two worlds at once. Since that is impossible, the פסוק must mean something else. רב will use it to show why being quoted matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will dwell in Your tent forever (in worlds)' (תהלים סא:ה)
Worlds, read here as two worlds: this world and the next
What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'I will dwell in Your tent forever (worlds)'?
But is it possible for a person
to live in two worlds?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִיפְשָׁר לְאָדָם לָגוּר בִּשְׁנֵי עוֹלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to step 12 with a difficulty in a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of 'אגורה באהלך עולמים'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person cannot live in two worlds at the same time, so the plural עולמים cannot be read literally.

steps.title: דוד asks to be quoted in this world
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means דוד asked that people say his Torah teachings in his name in this world after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, דוד said: Master of the World, let people say a teaching in my name in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק. דוד was asking to 'live' in this world even after death, by having his Torah repeated in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solves the two-worlds problem. דוד's soul is in the next world, but when people quote him, he is also present in this world. That is why being quoted by name matters, and why רב ששת cared.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World (a way of addressing ה׳)
A teaching that was heard and passed on
This world

phrases.english: Rather, David said:
Master of the World,
let them say a teaching in my name
in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר דָּוִד רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the difficulty of step 13 and so answers step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולמים would mean physically living in two worlds at once, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second 'world' is this world, where a person 'lives on' when his teachings are said in his name.

steps.title: A quoted scholar's lips move in the grave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that when a תלמיד חכם is quoted in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Any תלמיד חכם whose teaching is said in his name in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up דוד's request with a teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחי. It explains what actually happens to a scholar who is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why being quoted is like 'living' in this world: the scholar's lips move as if he were speaking again. It also explains רב ששת's reaction, since without credit he lost this.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar
His lips move, as if speaking
Grave

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the importance of saying a teaching in the name of the one who said it.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Any Torah scholar
in whose name people say a teaching
in this world,
his lips move in the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 by explaining how a quoted scholar 'lives' in this world.
steps.raayaObject: That being quoted in this world gives a scholar a kind of life here after death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי.

steps.title: The verse source: like a pile of grapes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר זעירי brings the פסוק 'דובב שפתי ישנים' and compares scholars to a pile of grapes that ooze when touched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר זעירי said: What is the פסוק? 'And your palate is like the best wine, going smoothly to my beloved, moving the lips of those who sleep.' Like a pile of grapes: just as a pile of grapes oozes as soon as a person touches it, so too with תלמידי חכמים: as soon as a person says a teaching in their name, their lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching and explains it with a picture of ripe grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those who sleep' refers to the dead, and 'moving their lips' refers to their lips moving when they are quoted. Ripe grapes in a pile ooze wine at the slightest touch. In the same way, just quoting a scholar is enough to set his lips moving.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (source verse)?
Moving the lips of those who sleep (שיר השירים ז:י)
A pile of ripe grapes left to soften before pressing
Touches

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת cared about credit because a scholar who is quoted by name 'lives on' in this world, and his lips move in the grave.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ze'eiri said:
What is the verse?
'And your palate is like the best wine,
going smoothly to my beloved,
moving the lips of those who sleep.'
Like a pile of grapes.
Just as a pile of grapes,
once a person touches it, it oozes,
so too Torah scholars:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָדָם אוֹמֵר דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּיו –
phrases.english: once a person says a teaching in their name,
their lips move in the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר זְעֵירִי מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the teaching in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a quoted scholar's lips move in the grave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים ז:י, 'דובב שפתי ישנים', explained through the image of a pile of grapes.

steps.title: Which ברייתא did רב ששת rely on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the halacha and asks which ברייתא רב ששת based his answer on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to רב ששת's answer about orphans' מעשר. It asks for the ברייתא that his answer was based on, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the משנה speaks about orphans' מעשר. The גמרא now wants the actual source that says orphans' מעשר may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: What is the baraita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story (steps 11-16) and returns to רב ששת's answer in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא behind רב ששת's answer about orphans' מעשר.

steps.title: Orphans' animal tithe may be sold
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold. When slaughtered מעשר is sold, the meat's value is folded into the price of the hide, fat, sinews, and horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: מעשר בהמה of orphans may be sold. And מעשר בהמה that one slaughtered: he folds its price into its hide, its fat, its sinews, and its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. It allows selling orphans' מעשר and explains how slaughtered מעשר can be sold without directly selling the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part is the source for רב ששת's answer: orphans' מעשר is an exception to the rule against selling מעשר, so the orphans do not lose out. The second part describes הבלעה: the meat itself is not priced, and the seller charges more for the hide, fat, sinews, and horns, which may be sold. How the two parts relate is disputed in the next steps by אביי and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal, which is holy
Orphans
He 'swallows it in,' folding the meat's value into another price
Its sinews

steps.confusionAlert: The second half of the ברייתא does not allow selling the meat of מעשר openly. The meat's value is hidden inside the price of the hide, fat, sinews, and horns. Whether this limit also applies to orphans is debated: אביי (step 20) says yes, and רבא (step 25) says orphans may sell normally.
steps.whatToRemember: Orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold so the orphans do not lose. This is the ברייתא behind רב ששת's answer. Exactly how it may be sold is debated next by אביי and רבא.

phrases.english: As it was taught: An animal tithe of orphans,
one may sell it.
And an animal tithe that one slaughtered:
he folds its value into its hide, its fat,
its sinews, and its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא that allows selling orphans' מעשר בהמה, with the price of slaughtered מעשר folded into the hide, fat, sinews, and horns.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's answer that the משנה speaks about orphans' מעשר, which may be sold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: 'מעשר בהמה של יתומים מוכרין אותו'.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא really saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means, because it seems to say two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says that orphans' מעשר בהמה 'may be sold,' which sounds like a normal sale. Then it talks about folding the meat's value into the price of the hide and other parts, which sounds like a special workaround. The גמרא wants to know how these two parts fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (asking for the meaning of a text that seems unclear or inconsistent)

phrases.english: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא seems to say both 'sell normally' and 'sell only through inclusion.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two parts of the ברייתא (a plain sale, and a sale through inclusion) fit together.

steps.title: אביי: Orphans may sell only through inclusion
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא is one rule: orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold, but only through הבלעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means. Orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold, but only by folding its value into the price of other parts.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The ברייתא is not giving two rules, only one: orphans may sell the meat, but only by folding its value into the price of other parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the ברייתא explains how the first half works. 'May be sold' does not mean a normal sale. It means a sale done through הבלעה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a corrected reading)
Orphans (here, young orphans who inherited the animal)
Folding the value of one item into the price of another

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, even orphans may not sell מעשר בהמה meat openly; they may sell it only through הבלעה. רבא disagrees in step 25.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This is what it is saying —
the animal tithe of orphans
may be sold through inclusion.
phrases.notes: The meat's value is folded into the price of the hide, fat, sinews and horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the two parts are one rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows a normal sale and also a sale through inclusion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows only one kind of sale for orphans: through inclusion.

steps.title: Why not let adults use inclusion, as with the לולב and אתרוג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that an adult may not sell through הבלעה, then asks how this differs from the משנה about buying a לולב in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that an adult may not sell even through inclusion. But how is that different from what we learned: someone who buys a לולב from his friend in שביעית gets the אתרוג as a gift, because he may not buy it in שביעית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first draws a conclusion from אביי's reading: since orphans get special permission, an adult may not use הבלעה. Then it starts a challenge using a case about a לולב and אתרוג. The challenge is finished in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If orphans need a special leniency, then a regular adult (a גדול) cannot use הבלעה at all. But the משנה about שביעית seems to allow a similar workaround for anyone. The אתרוג of שביעית may not be bought from an עם הארץ, so it is given as a gift instead.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: what we learn from the way something was said
An adult (here, an owner who is not an orphan)
What is the difference? (introduces a contradiction from a similar case)
The שמיטה year, whose produce may not be traded in the usual way
As a gift

steps.confusionAlert: The אתרוג is not given as a gift because the seller is generous. It is a gift because selling שביעית fruit to this buyer is not allowed.

phrases.english: Does this imply that for an adult, even through inclusion, it is not allowed?
What is different from that which was taught:
one who buys a lulav from his fellow in the Sabbatical Year —
he gives him an etrog as a gift,
since he is not permitted to buy it in the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: Source: משנה סוכה ג:יא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּגָדוֹל בְּהַבְלָעָה לָא? מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from אביי's reading and starts challenging it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that an adult may not sell מעשר בהמה through הבלעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In שביעית, a forbidden sale is avoided by a workaround, so a workaround should also work for an adult's מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רב הונא: Fold the אתרוג's price into the לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls רב הונא's ruling that if the seller won't give the אתרוג as a gift, he may fold its price into the לולב. This completes the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: if he did not want to give it as a gift, what then? And רב הונא said: he folds the price of the אתרוג into the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It brings רב הונא's ruling that the seller may simply charge more for the לולב to cover the אתרוג, which is exactly הבלעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא openly allows הבלעה for anyone in the שביעית case, not only for orphans. So why should an adult be forbidden to do the same with מעשר בהמה? This sharpens the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (introduces an earlier discussion about a source)
He folds in, includes the price of one item within another
An אמורא who rules on the לולב case

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מַאי?
phrases.english: if he did not want to give it to him as a gift, what then?
And Rav Huna said:
he includes for him the price of the etrog in the lulav!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks this as the punch of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: לֹא רָצָה לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מַאי? וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 21 by showing that הבלעה is allowed in the שביעית case.
steps.raayaObject: That הבלעה is permitted for anyone, so an adult should also be allowed it for מעשר בהמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling on the משנה in סוכה about buying a לולב in שביעית.

steps.title: With the לולב the trick isn't obvious; with מעשר it is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that folding the אתרוג's price into the לולב is not noticeable, but folding the meat's value into the hide and horns is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the matter is not evident. Here, the matter is evident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why הבלעה works for the לולב but not for an adult's מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לולב prices go up and down, so a high price does not look like a hidden sale of the אתרוג. But hide, sinews and horns are cheap, so a big price for them clearly shows that the meat is being sold. A workaround that obviously looks like a forbidden sale is not allowed, except for orphans, who get a special leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the case being compared)
Here (the case under discussion)
The matter is evident; anyone can see what is really going on

steps.whatToRemember: Within אביי's reading, הבלעה is allowed only when the hidden payment is not obvious. For an adult's מעשר בהמה it is obvious, so it is not allowed. רבא later reads the ברייתא differently and allows an adult to use הבלעה (step 25).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for workarounds: a legal trick is only acceptable if it does not openly look like the forbidden act.

phrases.english: There, the matter is not evident,
phrases.notes: A לולב's price can naturally vary.

phrases.english: here, the matter is evident.
phrases.notes: A high price for hide and horns clearly hides the price of the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 21–22 by showing a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) by how obvious the hidden payment is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since הבלעה works for the לולב and אתרוג, it should work for an adult's מעשר בהמה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: הבלעה works only when it is not noticeable. With מעשר בהמה it is obvious, so an adult may not use it.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא say it twice?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's reading. If the ברייתא describes only one case, why does it repeat the words 'מעשר בהמה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If so, why do I need the words 'animal tithe' two times?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation from Step 20. He uses the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the ברייתא teaches one rule: orphans may sell, but only through הבלעה. רבא notices that the ברייתא mentions 'מעשר בהמה' twice. A repeated subject usually signals two separate cases, so אביי's single-case reading does not fit the text.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem with what was just said)
Two times
Why do I need it? (asks why words seem extra)

phrases.english: Rava said: If so,
phrases.notes: Refers to אביי's one-case reading.

phrases.english: why do I need 'animal tithe' twice?
phrases.notes: The repetition suggests two separate cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה תְּרֵי זִמְנֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer (Step 20) on textual grounds.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of the ברייתא as a single rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double mention of 'מעשר בהמה' only makes sense if there are two separate cases.

steps.title: רבא reads the ברייתא as two cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that orphans sell the meat normally, while an adult's slaughtered מעשר בהמה may be sold only through הבלעה into the hide, fat, sinews and horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what it means: orphans' animal tithe may be sold in the normal way. An adult's animal tithe that was slaughtered may be sold only by folding its price into its hide, its fat, its sinews and its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading of the ברייתא. Each mention of 'מעשר בהמה' gets its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case one: orphans may sell the meat openly. Case two: an adult may sell it only by hiding the meat's value inside the price of the parts that may be sold, such as the hide and horns. So the leniency for orphans is now bigger than אביי said: they need no הבלעה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (young heirs)
In its normal way, openly
An adult owner
He folds (hides) its price into something else
Its hide, fat, sinews and horns

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say an adult may sell the meat outright. The adult may sell only through הבלעה. Only the orphans may sell 'כדרכו', openly.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: this is what it is saying,
phrases.notes: Introduces the new reading.

phrases.english: an animal tithe of orphans
phrases.notes: First mention, first case.

phrases.english: one may sell it in its normal way,
phrases.notes: No folding needed.

phrases.english: and an animal tithe of an adult that he slaughtered
phrases.notes: Second mention, second case.

phrases.english: he folds its price into its hide, its fat, its sinews and its horns.
phrases.notes: Sale only through הבלעה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's own challenge by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as two distinct cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא teaches one rule about orphans selling through הבלעה (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: Orphans may sell openly; an adult may sell after שחיטה only through הבלעה.

steps.title: רבא's source: the פסוק of תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק that puts תמורה right next to 'it shall not be redeemed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? As it is written: 'Then both it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to prove that an adult may sell the meat through הבלעה after שחיטה. Here he quotes the פסוק; the next step explains how it proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא read 'לא יגאל' as a ban on selling מעשר בהמה. Because the same פסוק also mentions תמורה, the two laws are linked. Whatever limits apply to תמורה will apply to the selling ban as well.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces one's own source)
Substitute: trying to swap a holy animal for a regular one
It shall not be redeemed (here: may not be sold)

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: רבא introduces his source.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Then both it and its substitute
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:לג

phrases.english: shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'
phrases.notes: The selling ban sits next to תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural basis for רבא's ruling in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That selling an adult's מעשר בהמה after שחיטה is not a Torah prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כז:לג, which puts תמורה next to 'לא יגאל'

steps.title: Torah bans selling only while alive; after שחיטה it is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: תמורה works only while the animal is alive, so the selling ban also applies only while it is alive. After שחיטה, the ban is only a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it make a substitute? While alive. When may it not be redeemed? While alive. So after שחיטה it may be redeemed. It is the רבנן who decreed against it after שחיטה, because of the time before שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the פסוק proves his point. He uses the link between תמורה and selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since תמורה applies only to a living animal, the matching ban 'לא יגאל' also applies only to a living animal. So by Torah law the meat may be sold after שחיטה. The ban after שחיטה comes from the רבנן, who worried people would also sell the animal while it was still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: While (the animal is) alive
Redeemed (here: sold)
They (the רבנן) made a protective decree
Because of (a concern about) another case

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step. Because the ban after שחיטה is only rabbinic, the רבנן can limit it, and that is what makes room for הבלעה.

phrases.english: When does it make a substitute? While alive,
phrases.notes: No תמורה after death.

phrases.english: when may it not be redeemed? While alive,
phrases.notes: Same time limit, learned from the פסוק.

phrases.english: so after slaughter it may be redeemed,
phrases.notes: Torah law allows selling after שחיטה.

phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who decreed after slaughter,
phrases.notes: The ban after שחיטה is rabbinic.

phrases.english: because of before slaughter.
phrases.notes: The concern: selling a live animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from Step 26 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: Selling after שחיטה is permitted by Torah law and banned only by the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link in the פסוק between תמורה (which works only while alive) and לא יגאל

steps.title: The decree covers only what is valued while alive
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the rabbinic גזירה to the part of the animal that is valued while it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: For something that is appraised while the animal is alive, the רבנן decreed after slaughter because of before slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to define how far the רבנן's decree goes. This line sets up his next move: explaining why the hide, fat, sinews and horns are not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live animal's price is based on its meat. So the רבנן banned selling the meat even after שחיטה, because it looks like selling the live animal. This suggests that parts not valued while alive were never included in the גזירה, which is why הבלעה into them works.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is appraised (valued)
The רבנן decreed

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law the meat of מעשר בהמה may be sold after שחיטה. The רבנן banned it only for the part valued while the animal is alive, its meat. That is why an adult may still fold the meat's price into the hide and horns.

phrases.english: An item that is appraised while alive —
phrases.notes: The meat, which sets the animal's value.

phrases.english: the Rabbis decreed after slaughter
phrases.notes: Ban on selling it after שחיטה.

phrases.english: because of before slaughter,
phrases.notes: The thought continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rabbinic decree described in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rabbinic ban on selling after שחיטה applies only to what is appraised while the animal is alive, its meat.
